newsitem.title: INDIA: India markets worry over Chidambaram cabinet role.
newsitem.headline: India markets worry over Chidambaram cabinet role.

text.p: While India ponders who will succeed caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, investors are more concerned about whether Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will keep his job, equity analysts said on Wednesday.

The Congress party has said it will support the minority United Front coalition again if the premier steps aside, and Deve Gowda's partners in the alliance are to meet on Thursday to choose his successor.

The emergence of G.K. Moopanar, head of the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) to which Chidambaram belongs, as a frontrunner has raised fears that the other 14 coalition partners will object to the southern-based TMC holding two top cabinet posts.
"I can't see how the United Front would agree to having the PM and finance minister from the same party," said one market strategist at a local brokerage.
Moopanar and Chidambaram are both former Congress party stalwarts who defected last year to form a regional party in Tamil Nadu, which is a junior constituent in the UF coalition.
But a New Delhi analyst did not see a problem.
"Moopanar should be able to retain Chidambaram as the finance minister, bringing back confidence among market players," S.C. Juneja of brokers Jaico Credit told Reuters.

Analysts say Moopanar is reasonably popular with industry, has a comfortable equation with Congress -- which toppled Deve Gowda's government last week when it pulled its key support -- but lacks administrative experience.
Foreign Minister I.K. Gujral, another hopeful for the top job, may be more acceptable to the markets, ensuring that Chidambaram held onto the finance portfolio, analysts said.
"Gujral is less controversial, more polished and has a wealth of administrative experience," said Maulik Sharedalal, a member-broker at the Bombay Stock Exchange.
Gujral, who belongs to the Janata Dal party, would also ensure that Chidambaram retained his portfolio, analysts said.
The coalition's Steering Committee is to meet at 3 p.m. (0930 GMT) on Thursday to choose the new premier.
Analysts said the stock markets would be steered by the new finance minister more than the next prime minister.
"The markets will go by who's the finance minister," said Antony Sequeira, managing director at Arcadia Share and Stock Brokers.
If Chidambaram, the architect of a widely acclaimed tariff and tax-cutting budget, retains the finance post the market will boom, he said.
The Bombay stock market could gain 50-60 points if Moopanar becomes premier, but the real thrust will not occur until the it becomes clear who will emerge as finance minister, Sharedalal said.
Major Indian exchanges were closed on Wednesday for a Hindu religious festival. The Bombay Stock Exchange top 30 index closed on Tuesday at 3,647.44, up 52.72 points.
Parliament is to debate Chidambaram's pro-business budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), held hostage by the three-week old political crisis, for three days starting April 21.
